questions.text: For a host machine that uses the token bucket algorithm for congestion control, the token bucket has a capacity of 1 megabyte and the maximum output rate is 20 megabytes per second. Tokens arrive at a rate to sustain output at a rate of 10megabytes per second. The  token bucket is currently full and the machine needs to send 12megabytes of data. The minimum time required to transmit the data is _____seconds.
questions.solution:
Bucket starts full (1 MB). While it drains, the host sends at 20 MB/s while tokens arrive at 10 MB/s:
[latex]20t=1+10t\Rightarrow t=0.1[/latex] s, sending 2 MB.

The remaining 10 MB go at 10 MB/s = 1 s.

Total = 0.1 + 1 = 1.1 s

Answer: 1.1

questions.text:
An IP datagram of size 1000 bytes arrives at a router. The router has to forward this packet on a link whose MTU (maximum transmission unit)is 100bytes. Assume that the size of the IP header is 20bytes.
The number of fragments that the IP datagram will be divided into for transmission is _________.
questions.solution:
Data = 1000 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 980 bytes. Per fragment: 100 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 80 bytes of data (already a multiple of 8).

Fragments = [latex]\lceil980/80\rceil=\lceil12.25\rceil=13[/latex]

Answer: 13

questions.text:
Consider that B wants to send a message m that is digitally signed to A. Let the pair of private and public keys for A and B be denoted by [latex]K_{x}^{-}[/latex]
 and [latex]K_{x}^{+}[/latex] for x = A,B, respectively. Let  [latex]K_{x}(m)[/latex] 
represent the operation of encrypting m with a key [latex]K_{x}[/latex] and H(m) represent the message digest. Which one of the following indicates the CORRECT way of sending the message m along with the digital signature to A?
questions.solution:
B signs by encrypting the digest with B's private key: [latex]K_B^-(H(m))[/latex]. A checks it with B's public key [latex]K_B^+[/latex] and compares with H(m).

Answer: {m, [latex]K_B^-(H(m))[/latex]}

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are example(s) of stateful application layer protocols?
(i) HTTP
(ii) FTP
(iii) TCP
(iv) POP3
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP is stateless (each request is independent).
- FTP keeps session state (login, current directory) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.
- TCP is a transport protocol, not application layer.
- POP3 keeps session state (authorization, transaction states) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.

Answer: (ii) and (iv) only

questions.text: Which one of the following protocols is NOT used to resolve one form of address to another one?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- DNS: hostname [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- ARP: IP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] MAC
- RARP: MAC [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- DHCP assigns IP configuration to hosts; it does not translate one address form into another.

Answer: DHCP
